stem: A school-aged child is reviewed for neurodevelopmental concerns and has a long face, large ears, hypermobility, and behavioural difficulties with autism spectrum features; which syndrome is most likely?
explanation: Fragile X syndrome is the most likely diagnosis. It classically causes intellectual disability or developmental delay, behavioural difficulties, autism spectrum features, a long face, large ears, and joint hypermobility.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because CHARGE syndrome is typically associated with coloboma, heart defects, choanal atresia, growth restriction, genital anomalies, and ear abnormalities.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because foetal alcohol syndrome usually causes a smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, growth restriction, and neurodevelopmental impairment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because neurofibromatosis type 1 is associated with café-au-lait macules, neurofibromas, axillary freckling, and learning difficulties.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because Fragile X syndrome classically presents with developmental delay or intellectual disability, autism spectrum features, behavioural difficulties, a long face, large ears, and hypermobility.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because tuberous sclerosis may be associated with autism, but it more typically presents with seizures, hypomelanotic macules, and other hamartomas.
